hypothesis.title: The Control Plane Under the Sound
hypothesis.question: Can a hidden routing layer make simple foreground material feel more inevitable, tense, and conversational than the same material without routing constraints?
hypothesis.hypothesis: If a two-minute study keeps its audible foreground simple but routes every transition through a hidden control plane—harmonic graph adjacency, isolated vocal-feature axes, chirp carriers, low-frequency pressure lanes, and 600 ms response windows—then listeners will rate the full-control version as more inevitable, tense, and conversationally alive than versions with the carriers or routing removed. The mechanism is nearest-accessible control: path constraints shape which musical states can crystallize next.
hypothesis.rationaleMd: S1 shows that physical systems may realize nearest accessible metastable phases rather than globally optimal states, with path/rate/timescale determining emergent form. S3 supplies a harmonic analogue: Tonnetz and related combinatorial configurations make chord identity and voice-leading adjacency explicit. S2 suggests a timbral control plane, where pitch, F2, intensity, noise, and higher-frequency characteristics can be manipulated as relatively isolated speech-feature dimensions. S5 adds a carrier model through chirp spread spectrum, where frequency-sweeping structure carries compressed voice through constrained channels. S6 gives a temporal control plane for full-duplex interaction, using 600 ms streaming chunks and warning that cascaded pipelines accumulate latency and information loss. S4 is more speculative, but supports the possibility that low-frequency/sub-audible acoustic causes can shape perceived presence or unease. Together, these sources support a composition whose foreground is governed by hidden routing signals rather than by surface repetition alone [S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6].

recipe.title: Control-Plane Composition Study
recipe.bodyMd: Create a 120-second study with simple foreground material but strict hidden routing. First, draw a 7-node chord graph and permit only adjacent moves, with section boundaries acting as high-pressure exceptions [S1, S3]. Second, build a vocal/formant pad with three separately automated axes: F0 or pitch, F2/formant position, and intensity/noise; move only one axis at a time in the first half, then two at a time in the second [S2]. Third, add a quiet chirp-like carrier—sine sweep, band-pass sweep, filtered noise ramp, or granular scan—300–600 ms before every harmonic move [S5]. Fourth, add a safe low-frequency pressure lane, preferably 24–36 Hz on ordinary monitors rather than unsafe true infrasound, swelling only at section crossings [S4]. Fifth, arrange call-and-response so answers begin within roughly 600 ms, preserving a full-duplex listening/speaking feel [S6]. Render Full Control Plane, No Carrier, and No Routing versions, then blind-rate inevitability, tension, and conversational aliveness.
dawChecklist: Draw a 7-node chord adjacency graph before writing notes.
Choose a starting node and write a progression using only adjacent moves except at section boundaries.
Create a vocal/formant pad with separate automation lanes for F0/pitch, F2/formant, and intensity/noise.
Automate only one vocal axis at a time in the first half; allow two-axis movement in the second half.
Place a quiet chirp, sweep, filtered-noise ramp, or granular scan 300–600 ms before every harmonic move.
Add a conservative 24–36 Hz pressure lane that swells only before section-crossing graph moves.
Arrange call-and-response gestures so each response begins within roughly 600 ms of the call ending.
Render Full Control Plane with all routing layers active.
Render No Carrier by removing chirps and the pressure lane while keeping notes and sounds constant.
Render No Routing by keeping sounds/carriers but allowing arbitrary chord jumps and loose response timing.
Blind-rate all renders for inevitability, tension, and conversational aliveness on a 1–7 scale.

protocol.listeningContext: studio headphones or monitors at conservative low-frequency playback levels; loudness matched before rating
protocol.listeningMethod: blind shuffled comparison with 1–7 ratings for inevitability, tension, and conversational aliveness
whatVaries: presence of chirp carrier and low-frequency pressure lane
